The two 24-month lines show the accumulated difference between observed monthly stroke or heart attack cases and the recent five-year pattern for the same event type. This makes broad departures easier to see while avoiding overinterpretation of individual weeks.

An upward slope means more cases than expected for that event type during that month; a downward slope means fewer. There is no reset at January 2023, so each final value represents the accumulated departure over the full two years.

Month-to-month variation should be treated as a surveillance signal rather than evidence of a change in population incidence. Counts describe hospital-registered events and may also reflect changes in case ascertainment, care-seeking and access to hospital services.
